invalid_failure_risks: Platform/ABI mismatch: ratelimit.so must be compiled for the exact container OS/arch (linux/amd64); if built on darwin/arm64 the .so won't dlopen, causing environment failure unrelated to solver skill
Timing flakiness: the characterization test ('delta ~1e9 in 100ms') and refill precision test ('wait exactly 1 real second') can fail under container CPU contention since 10x speed amplifies jitter

window_start_unix epoch conversion is underspecified in the instruction — solver must infer the unix offset formula; tests may be strict about the exact conversion, causing valid-looking solutions to fail
CGO + -race + dlopen has known edge cases in Go's race detector; false race reports or link failures on some toolchain versions could reject correct solutions

The instruction never explicitly states /metrics/ratelimit must be excluded from accepted+dropped counters — this appears only in internal hints, so a solver following only the instruction may reasonably include it and fail the consistency test through no ambiguity of their own making
review.reasons: The task has genuine multi-layer difficulty: an opaque plugin requiring experimental characterization, two interacting bugs at different code layers, and a cross-component consistency requirement that resists shallow fixes. Average score is 3.8 (above the 3.6 threshold) with no score below 3. The main risks are the platform ABI dependency of the pre-compiled .so and the undisclosed /metrics/ratelimit exclusion rule, both of which should be fixed before deployment.
fixes: Explicitly state in the instruction that /metrics/ratelimit requests must NOT be counted in requests_accepted or requests_dropped — this is a tested requirement currently hidden in internal hints only
Add a note in the environment spec confirming the .so is compiled for linux/amd64 and the verifier runs in a matching container, to eliminate ABI-mismatch invalid failures
Tighten the window_start_unix spec: define the exact conversion formula (e.g., 'unix seconds = server_start_unix + rl_now_ns()/1e8 / 1e9' or similar) so solvers aren't guessing at the epoch offset
Add a tolerance band to the timing-sensitive characterization test (e.g., assert delta is between 0.8e9 and 1.2e9) to reduce flakiness under container load
